quick.summary: Why a list of twenty usability problems gets ignored, and how to rank them.
quick.takeaway: Rank by how badly it blocks, and how many it hits.

beats.line: My usability report listed twenty problems. The team fixed the three easiest. Why?
Because all twenty looked equal. Rank them first.
Level one. People cannot finish the task at all.
Level two. They finish, but slowly or with mistakes.
Then note how many testers hit each one.
Less so when the levels are written down and you count testers.
Four of five could not pay. That goes first.
Now the worst problem is also the first one fixed.

quiz.question: Which usability finding should be fixed first?
options: Four of five testers could not complete payment
Two testers paused at a label, then continued
quiz.explanation: It blocks the task and affects most testers, so it has the highest severity and reach.

quiz.question: Rating usability findings by severity helps a team decide what to fix first.
quiz.explanation: A ranked list shows which problems stop people, so effort goes there before the easy cosmetic fixes.
